bibliographic.title: 100 Opportunities for More Inclusive Ocean Research: Cross-Disciplinary Research Questions for Sustainable Ocean Governance and Management
bibliographic.authors: Wisz MS, Satterthwaite EV, Fudge M, Fischer M, Polejack A, St. John M, Fletcher S, Rudd MA
bibliographic.citation_apa: Wisz, M. S., Satterthwaite, E. V., Fudge, M., Fischer, M., Polejack, A., St. John, M., Fletcher, S., & Rudd, M. A. (2020). 100 Opportunities for More Inclusive Ocean Research: Cross-Disciplinary Research Questions for Sustainable Ocean Governance and Management. Frontiers in Marine Science, 7, 576. https://doi.org/10.3389/fmars.2020.00576

methodology.method_family: horizon scanning synthesis with supplemental literature text analysis
methodology.study_design: three-part strategy: review horizon scanning literature, conduct text analysis of ocean science literature (1997-2017), formulate general policy-relevant questions
methodology.sample_description: 89 questions identified from major science and policy horizon scanning exercises, supplemented with 11 additional questions from broad ocean science literature scan
methodology.sector: marine and ocean science, policy, and governance
methodology.technology_context: ocean governance and management research agenda; no AI, LLM, or conversational systems

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The article synthesizes cross-disciplinary ocean policy and governance research questions; it does not address LLMs, generative AI, conversational systems, or governance mechanisms for such technologies.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Despite lexical overlap on terms such as governance, policy, law, and interaction, the study concerns sustainable ocean research agendas and marine environmental governance. No evidence in the provided text links the work to conversational AI, chatbots, agents, RAG, guardrails, or LLM deployment in regulated settings.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Topic mismatch is explicit in title, abstract, methods, and results; exclusion does not depend on ambiguous terminology.

appraisal.notes: Methodologically appropriate for a horizon-scanning synthesis in marine policy, but not transferable to conversational LLM governance. Limitations section not visible in provided excerpts.

cerqual.explanation: High internal coherence for ocean governance agenda-setting, but very low relevance to the review scope on conversational governance of LLM-based systems; no qualitative findings about AI governance mechanisms are present.

synthesis.main_claim: The authors synthesized 100 unprioritized, cross-disciplinary research questions intended to inform ocean policy and sustainable ocean governance.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a categorized inventory of ocean policy research questions drawn from horizon scans and supplemental literature review to guide the UN Decade of Ocean Science.
synthesis.limitations: Questions are general and unprioritized; contextual customization by ecosystem, region, and socio-political setting is required; limitations section not evidenced in provided excerpts.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude from the conversational LLM governance evidence base; governance and policy terms reflect marine environmental governance, not AI or conversational system governance.
